title: Work IQ: Microsoft IQ as a unified intelligence layer for agents
summary: The roadmap facts and documented governance controls are supported, including the spending-policy update endpoint. claims.claim: Microsoft Learn describes Microsoft IQ as a unified intelligence layer for enterprise AI.
claims.quote: Microsoft IQ is a unified intelligence layer for enterprise AI—one where every agent and Copilot interaction is grounded in a shared, continuously evolving understanding of the organization.

claims.claim: The Microsoft IQ hub lists four capabilities: Work IQ, Fabric IQ, Foundry IQ and Web IQ.
claims.quote: Microsoft IQ brings together four interconnected capabilities:

claims.claim: Work IQ provides context about how employees work, including people, collaboration and workflows.
claims.quote: Work IQ provides live understanding of how employees work, with context on people, collaboration, and workflows.

claims.claim: Fabric IQ provides the live state of the business.
claims.quote: Fabric IQ provides the live state of the business, so agents understand business entities and their relationships, properties, actions, and rules.

claims.claim: Foundry IQ provides curated institutional knowledge.
claims.quote: Foundry IQ provides curated institutional knowledge on the context of policies, authoritative documents, and reusable knowledge bases.

claims.claim: Web IQ provides fresh intelligence from the web.
claims.quote: Web IQ provides AI systems and agents with fresh, real-world intelligence from across the web.

claims.claim: Work IQ is a workplace intelligence layer enabling agents to access and reason over organisational and business data, context and tools.
claims.quote: Work IQ is a workplace intelligence layer that enables agents to access and reason over organizational and business data, context, and tools.

claims.claim: Work IQ has permission-aware governance.
claims.quote: It continuously builds a semantic understanding across Microsoft 365 and external systems with built-in, permission-aware governance.

claims.claim: Work IQ API endpoints include A2A.
claims.quote: Work IQ API endpoints include A2A, a remote MCP server, and a REST API.

claims.claim: Work IQ API endpoints include a remote MCP server.
claims.quote: Work IQ API endpoints include A2A, a remote MCP server, and a REST API.

claims.claim: Work IQ API endpoints include a REST API.
claims.quote: Work IQ API endpoints include A2A, a remote MCP server, and a REST API.

claims.claim: Work IQ API spending and consumption are managed in the Microsoft 365 admin center at Copilot > Cost management.
claims.quote: In the Microsoft admin center, Copilot > Cost management, admins can monitor Copilot Credit consumption and manage spending associated with the supported services such as Cowork, running apps hosted on the Copilot Managed Runtime, and Work IQ API.

claims.claim: The Cost management dashboard supports policy alerts.
claims.quote: Configure policy alerts and user-level threshold notifications.

claims.claim: The Cost management dashboard reports consumption by service.
claims.quote: Review consumption by spending policy, user, group, agent, service, and funding source.

claims.claim: The Cost management dashboard reports consumption by agent.
claims.quote: Review consumption by spending policy, user, group, agent, service, and funding source.

claims.claim: Auto-apply new services is enabled by default on spending policies, allowing future supported services and agents to inherit a policy.
claims.quote: Spending policies can automatically apply to future supported Microsoft Copilot services and agents. The Auto-apply new services setting is enabled by default for spending policies.

claims.claim: Administrators can turn off Auto-apply new services to review future services before adding them.
claims.quote: Administrators can turn off the setting for policies where future services and agents should be reviewed before they're added.

claims.claim: The Work IQ enablement guide names a Global Administrator for the one-time setup.
claims.quote: A user with Global Administrator role for the one-time Work IQ setup

claims.claim: The one-time setup described by the enablement guide creates the Work IQ service principal.
claims.quote: This section creates the Work IQ service principal in your organization, which provisions the Work IQ resource so your applications can request tokens for it.

claims.claim: The MCP overview says the Work IQ service principal is created automatically on first use.
claims.quote: The Work IQ service principal is created automatically in the tenant when you use Work IQ for the first time.

claims.claim: Manual service-principal provisioning can be needed when configuring MCP policy before first use.
claims.quote: In some corner cases, such as configuring Work IQ MCP policy in the Microsoft 365 admin center before any MCP use in the tenant, the service principal might not exist yet and policy configuration can fail.

claims.claim: The initial Work IQ MCP policy control is tenant-level.
claims.quote: In the initial release, Work IQ MCP provides tenant-level policy control.

claims.claim: Per-user, per-app, per-agent and scenario-specific policy templates are not part of the initial MCP policy control surface.
claims.quote: Per-user, per-app, per-agent, or scenario-specific policy templates aren't part of the initial policy control surface.

claims.claim: The MCP policy guide says more granular controls might be added later.
claims.quote: More granular controls and policy templates might be added later based on customer requests, feedback, and usage.

claims.claim: A spending policy is updated with PATCH https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies/{id}.
claims.quote:
PATCH /copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies/{id}
PATCH https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies/3f9e2c1a-0000-0000-0000-00000000c21b

claims.claim: The PATCH request's periodLimit property changes the spending-policy limit.
claims.quote: In the request body, supply only the values for the properties to update. The following properties can be updated: displayName, periodLimit, perUserLimit, and billingMethods.

claims.claim: The Cost Management API is beta and subject to change.
claims.quote: APIs under the /beta version are subject to change.

claims.claim: Use of the beta Cost Management API in production applications is not supported.
claims.quote: Use of these APIs in production applications is not supported.

claims.claim: Creating a spending policy through the Cost Management API also requires the Billing Administrator or Global Administrator directory role.
claims.quote: Creating a spending policy also requires the Billing Administrator or Global Administrator directory role at runtime.

claims.claim: Copilot Credits spending-policy management and consumption monitoring are tenant-scoped controls.
claims.quote: The Microsoft 365 Copilot Cost Management API helps administrators govern and observe tenant consumption of Copilot and AI credits through Microsoft Graph, rooted at /copilot/costManagement.
